title: xargs
subtitle: Stdin words → command arguments — batch, per-item, null-safe, parallel

cards.meaning: Read args from stdin (blanks/newlines) and append them to a command
cards.notes: Default command is /bin/echo. Memory hook: stdin = list of words; xargs stuffs them onto a command.

cards.meaning: Join multiline input into one echoed line
cards.notes: No command given → echo. Many lines become one line of args.

cards.meaning: One command per input item; {} is the placeholder
cards.notes: Bare xargs cmd = one cmd with many args. -i = one cmd per item.

cards.meaning: Modern spelling of -i — replace {} once per item
cards.notes: Preferred on GNU xargs. Same idea as -i.

cards.meaning: Same as -i, but placeholder is T instead of {}
cards.notes: Custom replace string when {} is awkward or already used.

cards.meaning: Split on NUL, not whitespace — safe for spaces/quotes/backslashes
cards.notes: Quotes and backslashes are not special. Always pair with find -print0.

cards.meaning: Run up to 4 processes at a time (default is 1)
cards.notes: -P 0 = as many as possible (be careful). Speeds multicore work.

cards.meaning: find prints paths; xargs turns lines into command arguments
cards.notes: Other half of find -exec. Prefer -print0 | xargs -0 when names may have spaces.
